items.title: Jimmy Owens interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: it was me and Richard Williams, that was the trumpet section

ctx.x: And you were eighteen or so? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Yeah. But it was me and Richard Williams, that was the trumpet section, and Slide Hampton and Garnett Brown was in the trombone section. Let’s see. Hubert Laws was playing tenor saxophone. And I can’t remember who else was in the band. But I mean it was a great band. And Slide was very popular. He’d had a hit, kind of a hit at that time, called “Sister Salvation,” so we played all of this music. And that was one of the times of getting paid. Now all the time that I worked in the hospital I didn’t take any of the…
That’s a great story too. Your timing is impeccable.

items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was the fact tat I was playing next to him

ctx.x: The sound of the metal plates is good, yeah. Richard Williams, say something about Richard Williams.
Well, it was a great gig and all I did was I sat there most of the time and listened to Richard Williams play very well. I mean, I soloed also.
What is unique about Richard Williams?
